cases.description: When the evaluation path contains a single element "root", getEvaluationPath().getName(-1) should return that element. toString() must therefore return "root".
When the evaluation path contains multiple elements ["root", "child", "grandchild"], getName(-1) should return the last element "grandchild". toString() must return "grandchild".
When the evaluation path is empty (no elements), calling getName(-1) is expected to throw an IndexOutOfBoundsException. toString() should propagate this exception.
When the evaluation path’s last element is explicitly null, getName(-1) returns null. toString() should therefore return null.
When the evaluation path contains a single element that is an empty string, getEvaluationPath().getName(-1) returns "" and toString() must return the empty string.
When the evaluation path's last element consists only of whitespace, toString() should return that whitespace unchanged.
When the last element of the evaluation path is a numeric string, toString() must return the exact numeric string.
When the evaluation path ends with a string containing special characters, toString() should return the same special‑character string.
If getEvaluationPath() returns null, invoking getName(-1) causes a NullPointerException which toString() must propagate.
When the JsonNodePath implementation throws an IllegalStateException inside getName(-1), toString() should propagate that exception.
When the evaluation path contains a large number of elements (e.g., 1000) and the last element is "leaf1000", toString() must correctly return the last element regardless of path length.

When getEvaluationPath() returns a JsonNodePath whose getName(-1) implementation throws IllegalArgumentException (e.g., because the internal index handling is invalid), toString() must propagate the IllegalArgumentException.
When getEvaluationPath() returns a JsonNodePath that does not support negative indexing and throws UnsupportedOperationException from getName(-1), toString() should propagate that exception.
When getEvaluationPath() returns a JsonNodePath whose getName(-1) throws a generic RuntimeException (simulating an unexpected failure), toString() must propagate the RuntimeException unchanged.
